Before

 Order

This Criminal Appeal under Section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is preferred being aggrieved by the judgment dated 11.01.2017 passed in Session Case No.314/2015 by the Third Additional Session Judge, Indore whereby the appellant has been convicted under Section 376(2)(i)
of the IPC and Section 4 r/w section 3 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and in the light of Section 42 of the POCSO Act, 2012 the appellant has been sentenced only under Section 376(2)(i) of the IPC for 10 years R.I. and Rs.1,000/- fine with default stipulation of 3 months R.I.
2.

The facts of the case in brief are that the appellant was tried under Section 376(2)(i) of the IPC and Section 4 r/w Section 3 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and Section 506 Part-II of the IPC for committing penetrative sexual assault with child victim (PW-3) aged 13 years on the date of incident i.e. 03.09.2015 regarding which Crime No.981/2015 was registered at Police Station Rajendra Nagar, Indore.

3. The appellant abjured guilt and prosecution examined as many as 7 NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17371 2 CRA-1095-2017 witnesses including child victim (PW-3), her mother as PW-2, Head Master - Smt. Kavita Awasthi (PW-4), Medical Officer - Dr. Preeti Shah Bhandari (PW-1), Sub- Inspector - K.S. Solanki (PW-5), Sub-Inspector - Sangeet Bariya (PW-6) and Sub- Inspector - K.S. Soliya (PW-7).
4.
In examination under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 all the facts and circumstances were either denied or ignorance were expressed.
He advanced the defence that he is the brother-in-law of real sister of PW-2 and his sister-in-law i.e. sister of PW-2 is connived with PW-2 and he has been falsely implicated in the crime.
No evidence has been adduced in defence.

sentences.text: Appreciating the evidence, the trial Court assessed the age of child victim (PW-3) as 13 years and also found proved that PW-3 was subjected to penetrative sexual assault and attracted the presumption under Section 29 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and convicted and sentenced the appellant as per para 1 of the judgment.
6. Challenging the conviction and sentence, this appeal has been preferred on the ground that the F.I.R. is delayed by 12 days and delay has not been explained.

In F.I.R. and the statement under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 the only allegation was of attempt to rape whereas the trial Court has convicted the appellant for committing the rape and appellant has been acquitted from the charges of Section 506 Part-II of the IPC, accordingly, the prosecution case does not stand on the test of proof beyond reasonable doubt.
Heard.
7. Learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent/State has supported the conviction as well as sentence.
Perused the record.

8. Challenge to the age of victim (PW-3) and findings of the trial Court does NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17371 3 CRA-1095-2017 not requires interference as victim (PW-3) was 13 years old on 03.09.2015.
9. Now we come to the findings recorded by the trial Court that victim (PW-3) was subjected to the penetrative sexual assault.

10. The challenge to the finding is on the ground that First Information Report was lodged for attempt to rape and even the final report was submitted under Section 376 r/w 511 of the IPC and the delay is unexplained.
11. We re

- appreciate the testimony of victim (PW-3), her mother (PW-2) and Medical Officer - Dr.
Preeti Shah Bhandari (PW-1).

The victim PW-3 has stated that the appellant/accused committed penetrative sexual assault and when she tried to raise an alarm then the appellant/accused caused injury by inflicting the assault by fist.
She complained to the mother that she is not in a good health and thereafter she was taken to the hospital where she was medically examined.
The Medical Officer - Dr. Preeti Shah Bhandari (PW-1) found on examination of victim at 04:35 PM on 16.09.2015 that hymen of the victim was torned.
There was a bleeding from the vagina, tenderness was present and injury was painful.
She gave a positive finding that the victim was subjected to forceful intercourse in the report Exhibit-P/1.

The suggestion is given to the doctor that the injury may be caused during cycle ride but there is no suggestion to the victim that she sustained the injury on private parts when she was taking a ride of bicycle.
The statement of mother of the victim (PW-2) has corroborated the daughter (PW-3) and explained the delay in lodging the F.I.R.

Accordingly, the mention of attempt in FIR (Exhibit-P/3) and the statement recorded under Section 161 of the Cr.P.C. does not affect the testimony of PW-2 and the facts proved by the prosecution are sufficient to prove the fundamental Rakesh @ Kalu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114170661/
2 facts required for attracting the presumption under Section 29 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and the trial Court rightly attracted the presumption against the appellant.

sentences.text: The burden to rebut the presumption is heavy and the appellant/accused has not adduced any evidence.
Only explanation under examination in Section 313 of the Cr.P.C. that due to family dispute he has been falsely implicated is not sufficient to discharge this heavy burden.
Hence, the trial Court rightly convicted the appellant under Section 376(2)(i) of the IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
This conviction is affirmed.
13. Only minimum sentence has been imposed.
Accordingly, interference is not required in sentence.
Hence, this appeal being devoid of merit and is hereby dismissed.
14. Copy of the judgment be supplied to the appellant through the Superintendent of the concerned jail, Indore.
15. Record be remitted back to the trial court for information and compliance.
